title: Console access heatmap + approval flow prototype
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers with large organizations struggle to quickly understand who has effective access to sensitive Console actions (deploy, rollout, dedicated capacity changes). Current audit log is chronological and verbose; workspace/org owners need a quick visual way to triage risky access and approve temporary elevations.

Objective: Produce a high-fidelity prototype that combines a role/permission heatmap, contextual session playback, and a lightweight approval flow for temporary access requests. The prototype will guide engineering and PM decisions for the Console -> Settings -> Access page and the new Audit quick-inspector.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Heatmap shows effective access per role across top 12 Console actions with hover details (role bindings, inherited org permissions).
- Clicking a cell opens a session-inspector panel with a condensed chronological view plus an inline play button to show the sequence that granted access (e.g., group add -> role change -> SSO claim).
- Designers and PMs can demo an in-app request flow: user requests time-limited privilege -> owner authorizes with reason -> audit entry created with link to playback.
- Prototype validated in 3 stakeholder usability sessions with at least 80% success rate on the triage task within 2 minutes.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus on read & approve flows only; no permissions engine changes required. Engineering will implement back-end endpoints for effective-permissions and session reconstitution (ENG-4021).
- Mobile layout is out of scope for this sprint; desktop + narrow-tablet only.
- Must respect PII constraints: playback redacts token and secret fields; audit playback returns action labels, actor, timestamp, and resource id only.

Proposed screens and components: 
1) Access heatmap (grid): rows = roles + groups; columns = key Console actions (Deploy, Rollout, Change Billing, Add Node, Delete Model, Edit Policy, View Billing, Export Logs, Manage Dedicated, Create Workspace, Modify VPC, Rotate Keys). Cells encoded by color for effective access (None/Read/Write/Admin) with small badges for inherited or time-limited perms.
2) Cell inspector (drawer): top summary (role, effective perm, sources), middle timeline (compact session playback with play/pause scrub), bottom quick actions (request elevation, open policy editor, link to full audit log).
3) Request elevation modal: choose duration (1h, 8h, 24h, custom), reason, approver; shows estimated blast radius and impacted resources checklist.
4) Approval inbox in Console header (bell dropdown) showing pending requests with one-click approve/deny and templated reasons.

Accessibility & privacy considerations:
- Heatmap must be keyboard navigable and readable by screen readers; provide alternative textual summary export for policy reviews.
- Playback transcript must redact secrets and show masked identifiers with reveal only for owners.

Prototype artifacts: Figma frames + interactive prototype for the flow, and a short clickable demo for PM review. Engineering spec will include API contract for effective permissions and session reconstruction (ENG-4021).

Open design questions: 
- What is the canonical list of "key Console actions"? Need PM input (PM-1287).
- How to model inherited permissions from org -> workspace vs direct bindings without overwhelming the user? Proposed: show top two inheritance sources and a link to full binding list.

Metrics to measure post-launch: time to triage (median), requests approved within SLA, reduction in audit log search queries for "who has access" queries.

Acceptance demo: interactive Figma prototype walkthrough with PM and two SREs; show three scenarios: (1) inherited admin found via heatmap and revoked, (2) playback explains temporal role binding that caused access, (3) owner approves 4-hour elevation for an on-call engineer.
